- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts (first 5–7 days) — apply upward bias of 2–5% for first 7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days — apply downward correction of 2–4%.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust forecast to align with 30-day MA unless sentiment overrides.
- Sentiment volatility >0.2 in 3 consecutive days triggers lag correction: forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2% in final 3–5 days — add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is positive, or downward if negative.
